searchDocs.title: A line of sight check​
searchDocs.content: local rayLens = require(game.ReplicatedStorage.raylens) local function has_line_of_sight(from: Vector3, to: Vector3, target: BasePart): boolean local direction = to - from local result = workspace:Raycast(from, direction, nil) rayLens.draw(from, direction, result) return result ~= nil and result.Instance == target end   Draw every check while you are testing, but wrap the rayLens.draw line in a flag so it costs nothing when you switch it off.

searchDocs.title: Draw only the misses​
searchDocs.content: Usually the bug you are chasing is the cast that nothing was able to find, drawing only those keeps the screen easy to read.  local result = workspace:Raycast(origin, direction, nil) if result == nil then rayLens.draw(origin, direction, result) end

searchDocs.title: A cone that has vision​
searchDocs.content: Six rays fanned across the cone, redrawn every frame. This needs onDraw because the origin moves.  local rayLens = require(game.ReplicatedStorage.raylens) local RAYS = 6 local RANGE = 60 local HALF_ANGLE = math.rad(30) rayLens.onDraw(function() local character = game.Players.LocalPlayer.Character local root = character and character:FindFirstChild("HumanoidRootPart") if root == nil then return end local origin = root.Position + Vector3.new(0, 2, 0) local forward = root.CFrame.LookVector for i = 0, RAYS - 1 do local step = i / (RAYS - 1) * 2 - 1 local direction = (CFrame.Angles(0, step * HALF_ANGLE, 0) * forward) * RANGE rayLens.draw(origin, direction, workspace:Raycast(origin, direction, nil)) end end)

searchDocs.title: Visualising a shape cast​
searchDocs.content: Blockcast takes a cframe & a size, so draw the volume at its starting position and then the path it travelled.  local rayLens = require(game.ReplicatedStorage.raylens) local start = CFrame.new(0, 20, 0) local size = Vector3.new(4, 4, 4) local direction = Vector3.new(0, -40, 0) local result = workspace:Blockcast(start, size, direction, nil) rayLens.box(start, size) rayLens.draw(start.Position, direction, result)   The box shows the shape you cast, the ray shows where it ended up and between the two, a shape cast that hits the wrong thing usually explains itself.

searchDocs.title: Cleaning up​
searchDocs.content: rayLens.clear()   Everything RayLens created goes away, and the frame loop stops.

searchDocs.title: Options​
searchDocs.content: </> interface Options { color: Color3? -- Adornment colour, orange by default transparency: number?-- 0 is solid, 1 is invis thickness: number?-- Line thickness (studs) radius: number?-- Marker and sphere radius (studs) lifetime: number?-- Seconds a one call draw stays on screen alwaysOnTop: boolean?-- Draw through geometry zIndex: number?-- 1 or more to draw above parts shading: Enum.AdornShading?-- Volume shapes only, lines ignore it adornCullingMode: Enum.AdornCullingMode?-- Never stops long rays fading with distance } Styling for a draw call, if you dont add anything it just uses the defaults

searchDocs.title: DrawCallback​
searchDocs.content: </> interface DrawCallback {} Called once per frame while onDraw is running where dt is the time in seconds since the previous frame.

searchDocs.title: draw​
searchDocs.content: </> RayLens.draw( origin: Vector3 ,-- Where the ray started direction: Vector3 ,-- The vector you cast, its length is the ray length result: RaycastResult?,-- The cast result or nil for a miss options: Options?-- Styling, blank fields fall back to the defaults ) → () Draws an already casted ray, put the result you got from worldRoot:Raycast, a nil result is nothing, drawn at full length with no marker, so the absent marker is what tells you it missed, a result is drawn to its hit point with a marker on the surface normal

searchDocs.title: ray​
searchDocs.content: </> RayLens.ray( origin: Vector3 ,-- Where the ray started direction: Vector3 ,-- Direction and length options: Options?-- Styling, blank fields just go to the defaults ) → () Draws a ray before or without casting it, direction carries its own length, matches worldRoot:Raycast(o, d), so the same vector can be passed to both

searchDocs.title: clear​
searchDocs.content: </> RayLens.clear() → () Removes every drawn adornment and stops the loop

searchDocs.title: onDraw​
searchDocs.content: </> RayLens.onDraw( callback: DrawCallback?-- Called once per frame with the frame delta, or nil to stop ) → () Adds a per frame callback, while the one that's set the previous frame is cleared before each call, so it draws inside the callback to create a new picture every frame and never rely on a lifetime, put nil to stop

searchDocs.title: It draws and it does not cast​
searchDocs.content: draw takes a RaycastResult you already have, if you have not cast one yet, pass nil and RayLens draws the ray at full length with no hit marker.

searchDocs.title: One shot / per frame​
searchDocs.content: Call draw once and you get one ray that expires after the lifetime you set (in seconds), the default is 8. If you already draw something that moves, the suggested way is using onDraw. The callback runs on every frame and anything drawn inside it is cleared before the next call so you get a new picture each frame.  Example:  rayLens.onDraw(function() local camera = workspace.CurrentCamera local origin = camera.CFrame.Position local direction = camera.CFrame.LookVector * 100 rayLens.draw(origin, direction, workspace:Raycast(origin, direction)) end)   To stop it, just run rayLens.onDraw(nil) and rayLens.clear(), these drop everything and stops the loop.

searchDocs.title: Styling​
searchDocs.content: Every draw takes an unrequired options table, so anything you leave out uses the default values.  field	default	notescolor	orange	none transparency	0.2	none thickness	0.05	lines only radius	0.15	marker and spheres lifetime	8	seconds, one shot draws alwaysOnTop	true	draws through geometry zIndex	1	must be 1 or more to sit above parts shading	XRay	volume shapes adornCullingMode	Never	stops long rays fading out with distance

searchDocs.title: Install​
searchDocs.content: Wally:  [dependencies] raylens = "superdupernairobi/raylens@0.1.0"   Studio users: grab RayLens.rbxm from the latest release and insert it into ReplicatedStorage (or your packages folder).
